business_summary.text: JSW Dulux Limited (formerly Akzo Nobel India) makes decorative and industrial paints, including auto, marine and protective coatings.

call_points.text: Management maintains its endeavor of double-digit growth in both volume and value.
Underlying gross margin was closer to 39.5-40% before the two drags.
About 160 people added, mainly in R&D and field, lifting employee and travel costs.
₹55.9 Cr dividend from wholly owned ICI R&T, from last quarter's real estate monetisation.
Project Akshaya integration yielded ₹2.4 Cr of savings in Q1, part of a three-year roadmap.
Combined JSW Paints plus JSW Dulux is close to ₹6,000 Cr; ambition is number two in decorative and number one in industrial.
Competitive intensity to persist for 1-2 years with new entrants still discounting.
July demand was weaker on late rainfall; management expects the quarter in a similar band.
No FY27 number; management targets double-digit volume growth long term and flags possible margin compression for a quarter.
Decorative capacity utilisation is 55-60% and industrial 70-80%; cross-manufacturing between the two companies' plants has started.
The last real-estate sale completed in March 2026, adding ₹64.8 Cr of income.
Board approved a final dividend of ₹50 per share for FY26, subject to shareholder approval.
Management declined to quantify market-share gains, saying only that it is gaining at the cost of suppliers.
Asked about FY27 volume, management said the environment is unpredictable and it is doing scenario planning.
Dealer integration is limited to the projects business in 7 metros; retail integration is planned only for early next year.
Decorative paints saw a rebound in volume growth despite competitive pressure; retail and semi-urban geographies grew faster.
Price increases of ~10% were taken in March-May after Jan-Feb pricing corrections to reduce the premium in select categories.
Geographic expansion target of 6,000 towns by next year.
Royalty savings are being reinvested towards increased painter engagement and brand initiatives.
Final dividend of ₹50 per share recommended, subject to shareholder approval.
Industrial Paints: Marine & Protective Coatings achieved highest revenue in March; strong order growth in Oil & Gas, Infrastructure and dry dock.

On 12 August 2026 JSW Dulux's Q1FY27 call reported 18.8% like-for-like revenue growth to ₹965 Cr on 25% volume growth, with PAT of ₹135.5 Cr including ₹77.4 Cr of one-offs, and guided EBITDA margin back to 13-15%.
Madhya Pradesh GST Department issued an Appeal Order on 13 October 2026, annulling the demand of Rs. 77,13,373/-.
On 19 October 2026, JSW Dulux reported that the Karnataka GST Department reduced its FY21 demand order to ₹42.04 Cr.
